name: colour-coded waveform frequency climb
looks: A full-bleed colour field cuts through red, then yellow-green, then cyan, each time paired with a rising frequency value and a small spectrum bar showing where that colour sits on the scale. Under the number, a set of overlapping wave lines gets tighter and faster with every cut, and a small caption names the value as the rate at which the system takes in, decides, and responds.
build: The background hue hard-cuts between steps with no crossfade; two or three canvas sine waveforms have a frequency that scales with the step's value. A corner spectrum bar is a fixed gradient strip with a small marker tweening to the current wavelength; the number ticks with no easing (the spectrum-waveform-cycle mechanic).
sound: A tone that climbs in pitch with each cut, a soft chime landing on each new colour.
prompt: Cut through a few full-bleed colour steps, each paired with a climbing frequency number and a tightening, quickening waveform underneath, so a viewer reads one quantity, how fast the system senses and responds, through colour, number and line all moving together.
